summary: V. Venkatachalam was an Indologist who studied at the University of Madras, Nagpur University, and Vikram University. He served as Director of the Scindia Oriental Research Institute, Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research.

V. Venkayya was an epigraphist and scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He succeeded Eugen Hultzsch, serving as Acting Government Epigraphist of Madras and for the Archaeological Survey of India.

V. W. Paranjpe was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, succeeding Shripad Krishna Belvalkar, and was later attested as Professor Emeritus at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017 and held an attested post there in 2018.

Valdo H. Viglielmo was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Harvard, Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Gakushuin. He taught at Harvard, Princeton, and several universities in Tokyo, before serving as Professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1965 to 2002.
Valeria Gazizova is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who completed her master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne.

Valerie Stoker is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi. She holds a post at Wright State University.
Vamana was an Indologist who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale. He held posts at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University.

Vans Kennedy was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army from 1817 to 1835 and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from around 1835 to 1846.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev was a Sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the University of Saint Petersburg, the National Library of Russia, and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who studied at Kazan Federal University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski. He served as professor at Kazan Federal University and the University of Saint Petersburg, and joined the Imperial Academy of Sciences.

Vasily Radlov was a linguist, archaeologist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at Berlin and Jena. He worked at Barnaul District School, became a member of the Imperial Academy of Sciences, and directed the Kunstkamera from 1894 to 1918.
Vasily Seseman was a philosopher who studied at the University of Saint Petersburg. He held academic posts at the University of Saint Petersburg, Vytautas Magnus University, and Vilnius University.

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was Honorary Professor at Nagpur University.

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale was an Indologist, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn. He held professorships at Fergusson College and the University of Delhi, and taught at Visva-Bharati University.

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He held positions at the Government Museum in Mathura, State Museum in Lucknow, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Banaras Hindu University.

Vasudha Dalmia is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Delhi, Cologne, JNU, and Heidelberg. She taught at the University of Tübingen, was a professor emerita at UC Berkeley, and served as Professor of Hindu Studies at Yale University.

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned degrees from the University of Madras, University of Mumbai, and Harvard. She is a Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida and served as President of the American Academy of Religion.
